title: Rosacea Phenotype Treatment Algorithm
subtitle: Erythema, papules/pustules, phymatous disease, and ocular involvement

steps.prompt: Are ocular symptoms present: gritty eyes, blepharitis, conjunctivitis, keratitis symptoms?
Ocular rosacea: lid hygiene, topical/systemic therapy, ophthalmology if keratitis risk
steps.detail: Pain, photophobia, corneal symptoms or reduced vision warrant urgent ophthalmic assessment. Rosacea phenotypes can coexist. Evaluate and treat other present ocular and cutaneous features rather than treating this branch as mutually exclusive.

steps.prompt: Is phymatous thickening or rhinophyma present?
Phymatous rosacea: medical control plus procedural/surgical discussion
steps.detail: Rosacea phenotypes can coexist. Evaluate and treat other present ocular and cutaneous features rather than treating this branch as mutually exclusive.

steps.prompt: Are inflammatory papules or pustules present?
Papulopustular rosacea: topical ivermectin/metronidazole/azelaic acid ± oral doxycycline
steps.detail: Rosacea phenotypes can coexist. Evaluate and treat other present ocular and cutaneous features rather than treating this branch as mutually exclusive.

steps.prompt: Erythematotelangiectatic rosacea: trigger control, vasoconstrictor, laser/light discussion
steps.detail: Rosacea phenotypes can coexist. Evaluate and treat other present ocular and cutaneous features rather than treating this branch as mutually exclusive.

citations.quote: ROSCO 2019 recommends a phenotype approach for rosacea diagnosis, classification, and management.
Rosacea systematic review supports phenotype-led interventions including topical ivermectin/azelaic acid/metronidazole, doxycycline, laser/light, and ocular therapy.
